decisions.evidence: Read the definition against Schlumprecht Def. 3.1.1: uniqueness of the fixed-order expansion is included, coordinate functionals are algebraic only, and the boundary cases (zero vector, one-vector and empty bases, deliberate exclusion of rearrangement) are stated. The trace-boundary risk is the notation K=sup_N||P_N|| possibly infinite before boundedness; the text says this explicitly, so no continuity is smuggled in.

Statement-level check of the definition: P_N linear, finite-rank, idempotent, P_M P_N=P_min from coefficient uniqueness, and K=sup_N||P_N|| explicitly allowed to be +infinity before the boundedness theorem so no continuity is assumed.

Re-derived steps 1.1-5.1: definiteness from e_n!=0, fixed-coordinate Cauchy extraction via the finite-dimensional coordinate maps, the uniform-in-N estimate passed to l->infinity, and completeness by splitting a Cauchy tail into the a^(k) tail plus two 2*epsilon blocks. Checked the zero space, the empty representation, and that ||S||<=1 and bijectivity (existence/uniqueness of expansions) are correctly separated from continuity of S^{-1}, which is not claimed here.

Biconditional-free direct proof checked step by step. Step 1.1's only choice input is DC through thm-bounded-inverse-theorem, declared in [A1]/[L2]; step 2.1 verifies P_N=S Q_N S^{-1} including N=0 and the ||Q_N||<=1 truncation contraction; step 3.1 divides by ||e_n||!=0. K<infinity follows from ||P_N||<=||S^{-1}||.

Checked the countable dense set (finite combinations with rational, respectively Gaussian-rational, coefficients), its countability from the countable union over supports, and the two-step epsilon/2 approximation of an arbitrary vector via its basis expansion. Both scalar fields are covered and no choice is used.

Definition checked against Muger Appendix A: unconditional convergence is convergence of every permutation to the same sum, explicitly separated from absolute convergence and from the fixed-order series.

Definition checked: unconditional means every basis expansion converges unconditionally; conditional is the negation; the quantifier range is over all x and the note that the formal series sum_n e_n is not asserted is correct.

Checked all five conditions and every direction: 1.1's least-code recursion is choice-free, 2.1 (1)=>(3) uses the increments across each block F_k whose two endpoint positions both tend to infinity, 3.1 (3)=>(2) via a Cauchy net in the Banach space, 4.1 cofinality, 5.1 both equivalences with (3), and 6.1's layer-cake/convexity bound with the stated 4M (2M real) constant plus the multiplier-to-subseries step. Boundary: empty B, M=0, finite F.

Definition checked: compact-uniform approximation of the identity by bounded finite-rank operators, lambda-BAP adding ||T||<=lambda, no sequence of operators required; the remark lambda-BAP => AP matches the definition.

Verified the limit operator is bounded with ||T||<=M_0, the M=0 branch, and the 3-net estimate ||(T_n-T)x||<=M||x-x_j||+||(T_n-T)x_j||. The empty compact set C is vacuously covered by the displayed sup; the proof's net choice only needs C nonempty.

Checked that each P_N has finite rank and ||P_N||<=K, that pointwise convergence P_Nx->x is exactly the defining expansion, and that applying the compact-uniform lemma gives the K-BAP witness T=P_N with the same constant K; BAP=>AP is the definition. DC is the only choice input and it is inherited from the coordinate-boundedness theorem.
Definition checked: finite additivity only, variation as a supremum over finite partitions, ba as the finite-variation subspace, |nu|(empty)=0 from the empty-cell convention.
Checked both scalar fields: partition into cells of diameter below epsilon (real) and squares of side below epsilon/sqrt2 (complex), finite range of the resulting sequence, and the sup-norm estimate.
Definition checked: provisional partition formula only, with representation-independence and extension deferred to the next lemma; no countable-additivity claim is made.

Boundary cases checked: zero function, empty E, |nu|(N)=0, and nu=0. The isometry statement uses completeness of the scalar field (cited).
Checked Phi(phi)(A)=phi(1_A), finite additivity, the phase argument giving ||nu_phi||_ba<=||phi||, the finite-range identity, density, the inverse identity, and the isometry ||I_nu||=||nu||_ba.

Checked sublinearity of the Cesaro limsup functional, its agreement with the limit on convergent sequences, the single AC use via dominated Hahn-Banach, positivity, normalisation ||L||=1, and shift invariance from the telescoping identity.

Checked both directions: finite partial variation bounds for a_n=nu({n}), the absolutely convergent series form, countable additivity, and the proper-subspace witness built from the shift-invariant mean. The step 'finite additivity plus nu(N)=1 force c=0' uses positivity of the mean, which is part of the supplier's statement, and I verified the equality of all singleton masses under the shift S1_{n}=1_{n-1}.

Checked steps 1.1-6.1: every bounded finite-rank operator is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank finite-expansion operators (finite basis of the range, bounded coefficient functionals, dense generator); |a_kk|<=||T||_(M) from property A; vanishing of the localized traces on far disjoint blocks; the telescoping bound |1-Tr~(M_m,T)| >= 1 - K||T|| sum_{k>=m} 1/log|M_k| with C=K/(1-a^{-1}); the limit passage to arbitrary bounded finite-rank T; and the contradiction with lambda-BAP from the compact unit ball of the finite-dimensional [M_m].

Repaired. Statement item 3 rendered the relation as the bare token 'le' so the estimate did not display an inequality; replaced by \le after checking the estimate itself (complement identity of item 4, binomial recurrence at |a|=2, and the endpoint cases |a|=1,2,2n-2,2n-1). Repaired and source-verified. The authoritative English Acta scan (Enflo, Acta Math. 130 (1973), p.315) gives conditions 4-6 exactly: |N_{m,i} cap N_{m,j}| <= 2t_{m+1}/n_{m+1} for i != j; |N_{m,j} cap M_{m,i}| <= min(t_{m+1}/n_{m+1},t_m/n_m); and total multiplicity error <= 1/n_{m+1}. The first two had both been mistranscribed. Step 6.1 now reproduces Lemma 7's norm comparison: condition 4 controls the other middle-block components by 2/n, condition 5 controls the two outer blocks by 1/n, and the Hilbertian norm is <2 times the norming component, yielding 4||T||/n. Steps 7.1-8.2 now reproduce Enflo pp.316-317: L_m=floor(k_m/t_{m+1}), nu_m=floor(k_{m+1}/(L_m t_m)), balanced multiplicities prove condition 6, intersections are spaced by at least t_m/nu_m, and t_m/nu_m=t_m^{gamma+2-alpha(gamma+1)+o(1)}>n_{m+1} because alpha<(gamma+2)/(gamma+1), proving the exact condition 4. The earlier Walsh-layer label repair remains correct. Focused precheck, rendercheck, and strict proof-contract checks pass. Owner reread of Enflo p.314 also exposed that the prior property-A paragraph proved only a one-component coefficient bound, while the local definition requires the factor ||e_k||. Step 4.1 now proves the inequality in every C(K_r) coordinate where e_k is nonzero and aggregates those inequalities in the Hilbertian sum, giving the full generator norm; this closes p2-next18-b1-owner-enflo-property-a-full-norm.

Checked the tensor-norm hierarchy, the vector density fact for reflexive range, N=PI=I for reflexive X, the AP kernel removal, the trace duality isometry, weak-operator density of finite-rank contractions by the bipolar theorem, and the compact-set upgrade to MAP; AC uses itemized.

Accepted after independent supplier repair and recertification. The repaired Walsh-block assembly now proves the logarithmic finite-rank lower bound from Enflo's exact conditions 4-6 and source spacing argument. This theorem's own inference remains sound: that bound excludes every finite BAP constant; reflexivity plus AP gives MAP by the local Grothendieck theorem and hence contradicts no-BAP; a Schauder basis likewise gives BAP under DC (available from AC). The constructed generator is nonempty, so the zero-space case is excluded. No supplier gap remains.
